text:
Luke Schenn came into this season with 1,122 NHL games and two Stanley Cup rings from Tampa Bay, and he's back in Vancouver for a third stint. The role is familiar: third-pair minutes (12.9 a night), a lot of contact (34 hits in 11 games) and very little shooting. Two assists so far.

The hard part is the five-on-five picture. With Schenn on the ice, the Canucks get just 35% of the expected goals, our measure of chance quality, and they've lost nine of the last ten games he's dressed for. That's a team problem as much as his, but it isn't a new pattern: Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season (-0.7 wins), with his team creating less offense with him out there than almost any other defenseman's (bottom 1%).

At 37, he's also near the bottom of the league in top-end skating speed (5th percentile by NHL EDGE). What Vancouver gets is experience, a right shot and a player who will drop the gloves (one fight already). Our hunch is that his minutes shrink before they grow, unless the Canucks' results turn and the coaches want a steady veteran over a puck mover.
headline: Luke Schenn, two Cups in, on a hard shift
